page.title: The component library
page.description: Every example below is the live component, rendered from the same code that ships. Each entry documents its keyboard and screen reader contract, because a component that looks right but cannot be operated without a mouse is not finished.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Heading level and visual size are separate props. Choose the level for document structure, then the size for appearance — so an outline is never broken to satisfy a layout.

content.heading: A level-2 heading rendered at visual size 3
content.lead: Lead paragraphs use Amalia Light at 22px. The lighter weight at a larger size keeps an introduction distinct from body copy without resorting to colour.
content.body: Body copy is Amalia Regular at 16px with a 1.6 line height. It never drops below 16px, and the measure is capped at 68 characters so long-form reading stays comfortable.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.description: There is exactly one primary action per view, and it is always yellow with off-black text. Secondary — the off-black outline — is the workhorse for everything else.

sizes.title: Sizes, icons and state
sizes.description: Icons are always decorative and paired with a text label, or the button carries an aria-label. The default 44px height meets the WCAG 2.2 target-size minimum.

a11y.tab: Moves focus to the button; a 2px off-black ring appears with a 2px offset.
a11y.space: Activates the button. Native button semantics are preserved.
a11y.ariaBusy: Set while loading. The control stays in the tab order and a visually hidden status describes the operation, so focus is never lost mid-submit.

forms.title: Form controls
forms.description: Every control has a visible, programmatically associated label. Help text and error text are wired through aria-describedby, and errors are announced rather than only coloured.

a11y.tab: Moves between controls in DOM order, which matches visual order.
a11y.space: Toggles a checkbox or switch; selects the focused radio option.
a11y.arrowKeys: Moves between radio options and within an open select listbox.
a11y.ariaInvalid: Set on a field that fails validation, with the message referenced by aria-describedby and rendered in a live region.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.description: Status is never carried by colour alone: each tone has a distinct icon and a text label, so meaning survives greyscale and colour-vision deficiency.

callouts.title: Callouts
callouts.maintenanceBody: Online banking will be unavailable on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 CET.
callouts.paymentBody: Your transfer of EUR 12,500.00 has been accepted for processing.
callouts.verificationBody: Two documents are still required before this account can be activated.
callouts.transferBody: The beneficiary IBAN could not be validated. No funds have left your account.

data.title: Data display
data.description: Enterprise screens live or die on tables. Headers use scope, numeric columns are right-aligned and tabular, and the caption describes the table for screen reader users.

table.title: Table
table.caption: Recent transactions with counterparty, date, status and amount

disclosure.title: Disclosure and navigation
disclosure.description: Tabs and accordions are the two approved ways to divide dense content. Both are keyboard-complete and expose their expanded state to assistive technology.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.overviewBody: A summary of the mandate, its signatories and the products in scope.
tabs.limitsBody: Daily and per-transaction limits by product and by authorised user.
tabs.documentsBody: Signed mandates, KYC evidence and the current fee schedule.

accordion.title: Accordion
accordion.a1: For the logo, the single primary action in a view, and deliberate brand moments such as a hero panel or a statistic. It is not a background for dense content and never a text colour.
accordion.a2: Set data-surface="inverse" on a wrapper. That reassigns the semantic colour tokens for the whole subtree, so components inside become brand-correct without any dark variant.
accordion.q3: Can I add a colour that is not in the palette?
accordion.a3: No. Add a semantic token that aliases an existing primitive instead. If a genuinely new value is needed, it goes through brand governance and lands in the primitive layer first.

a11y.arrowKeys: Moves between tabs in the tab list; the panel follows automatically.
a11y.tab: Moves from the active tab into its panel, skipping inactive tabs.
a11y.enterSpace: Toggles an accordion item; aria-expanded reflects the new state.

overlays.title: Overlays
overlays.description: Dialogs trap focus, restore it to the trigger on close, and are dismissible with Escape. Every dialog has a title that names it for assistive technology.

dialog.title: Dialog
dialog.confirmDescription: Revoking removes all authorisations for the four signatories on this account. Pending instructions will be cancelled. This cannot be undone.

a11y.escape: Closes the dialog and returns focus to the element that opened it.
a11y.tabShiftTab: Cycles within the dialog only; the page behind is inert.
a11y.roleDialog: Labelled by its title and described by its description, both wired automatically.

surfaces.title: Surface contexts
surfaces.description: The same markup, four times, with only the data-surface attribute changed. No component below knows which context it is in.
surfaces.heading: Make it happen
surfaces.body: Body copy, a secondary tone, and controls — all resolved from the semantic tokens that this surface context reassigns.

formExample.title: Payment form
formExample.description: A realistic control set: text input with help text, a live validation error, a select, a textarea, checkbox, radio group and a switch.
formExample.ibanHelp: Enter the full IBAN without spaces. Required fields are marked with an asterisk.
formExample.executionExpress: Express — same day, additional fee applies
formExample.confirmLabel: I confirm the beneficiary details are correct
formExample.notifyLabel: Email me when this payment settles

navigationSection.title: Navigation
navigationSection.description: The three navigation surfaces an enterprise screen needs: a sidebar for the application, a breadcrumb trail for depth, and pagination for long result sets.

sideNav.title: Side navigation
sideNav.description: Sectioned, collapsible sidebar navigation that lives in normal document flow, so it can be a page rail or the left column of a dashboard shell. Collapsing leaves a labelled icon rail rather than hiding the navigation.

drawer.title: Drawer navigation
drawer.description: The same navigation model on a small screen: a sheet from the left edge, focus-trapped and dismissible with Escape.

a11y.ariaCurrent: Set on the active sidebar item, the current breadcrumb page and the current page in pagination, so position is never carried by colour alone.
a11y.enterSpace: Activates a sidebar item; on a group it toggles the disclosure and updates aria-expanded.
a11y.escape: Closes the drawer variant and returns focus to the trigger.

dock.title: Centred dock
dock.description: A pill-shaped switcher that hugs its content instead of spanning the container — used where a few sibling views share one screen.

statisticsSection.title: Statistics
statisticsSection.description: One statistic component, four treatments. Each one inherits the surrounding surface context, so the inverse band, the light dashboard tile and the corporate panel are the same component — not four copies.
statisticsSection.subsectionDescription: Only the surface context changes below. No statistic knows which section it is in.

a11y.grouping: A StatGroup is a labelled region, so a screen reader announces the band before reading the figures.
a11y.trend: Direction is carried by an arrow icon and a signed number, not by red and green alone.
a11y.numerals: Figures use tabular numerals so a column of numbers stays aligned when values change.

statusSection.title: Status and progress
statusSection.description: The small parts every screen ends up needing: determinate progress, loading placeholders, identity and a hint on hover or focus.

avatar.title: Avatar, separator and tooltip
avatar.name: Hana Mahmutović
avatar.tooltip: Appears on hover and on keyboard focus, and stays while pointed at.

a11y.roleProgressbar: Progress exposes its value; the visible percentage is duplicated in the accessible name.
a11y.skeletons: Marked aria-hidden and paired with a polite live region elsewhere, so loading is announced once rather than as a wall of empty boxes.
a11y.focus: Tooltips open on keyboard focus, not only on hover, and never contain interactive content.

dashboard.label: Dashboard
dashboard.description: 4 metrics + chart + activity rail. Back office.

contrastChecker.passesAllAa: This pair clears every AA threshold, including small body text.
contrastChecker.failsAa: This pair fails at least one AA threshold. Check the rows below for where it may still be used.

bodyText.label: Body text
bodyText.description: Text below 24px, or below 19px when bold — SC 1.4.3 / 1.4.6.

largeText.label: Large text
largeText.description: Text from 24px, or 19px bold and above — SC 1.4.3 / 1.4.6.

uiComponent.label: UI and graphics
uiComponent.description: Borders, icons, focus rings and control boundaries — SC 1.4.11.
